jobs.title: Litigation strategist / Commercial litigation / Mass arbitration attorney
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Role

We're hiring a plaintiff-side litigation attorney to help drive Chariot's growing mass arbitration docket. You'll work with our legal strategy product team, ops team and outside counsel to initiate, prosecute, and resolve consumer arbitration cases across multiple sub-theories including but not limited to UDTP, privacy, data breach, and false advertising. Cases span household-name defendants and tens of thousands of claimants per campaign. You must be comfortable using legal tooling, AI and automation.

About Chariot Claims

Chariot Claims is an AI claims agent that helps consumers get paid for every corporate violation impacting them—data breaches, privacy violations, antitrust, and more. We’ve processed 65,000+ claims, with projected consumer recovery of $75M+.

Chariot builds technology to challenge the status quo. We take bold swings at the system to ascertain truth from stories, even if that means drawing legal/PR fire from established actors who are territorial and profit from the status quo.

As operators, we pride ourselves on our ethics, resilience, and humanity. With each turn, we emerge smarter, better prepared, and with more insiders who share our mission to build a better system. We’re already working with 20+ law firms, including several among the five most active complex litigation firms in the country.

Key Responsibilities

  • Improve Chariot's case evaluation playbook — design the framework, run reviews, and codify it for scale and repeatability

  • Partner with co-counsel to run plaintiff-side mass arbitration campaigns end-to-end: pre-suit demands, notices of dispute, AAA/JAMS filings, IDRs, and settlement negotiations

  • Serve as Chariot's internal authority on case strategy, redlines, and substantive filings

  • QA demand letters, notice batches, and claimant communications pre-send

  • Evaluate and validate new case theories across consumer protection, privacy, and complex litigation verticals

Who You Are

  • JD and active bar membership in at least one U.S. jurisdiction

  • 5+ years of plaintiff-side litigation experience, ideally at a mass arb / consumer class action firm — backgrounds at firms like Gutride Safier, Lieff Cabraser, Grant & Eisenhofer, or similar plaintiff-side shops are an ideal fit

  • Direct experience with consumer protection, UDTP, privacy/wiretapping, data breach, and/or false advertising theories

  • Comfortable with high case volume and legal tooling/technology (AI, Automations)

  • Deadline-driven, organized, and pragmatic; able to make calls quickly without losing rigor

Why Join Us?

  • Massive Greenfield opportunity to build the litigation function inside a fast-growing legal tech company

  • Competitive salary, equity, and benefits package in a fast-growing, high-impact startup

  • Collaborative, smart, humble, mission-driven, high-vibes team that loves music

  • 2-4 off-sites per year in beautiful, cultural destinations; expenses covered for you and a +1.

Position Type: PT or FT Contract to Hire or W2 Full-Time (Flexible)
Location: Remote

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
ABOUT CHARIOT CLAIMS

Chariot Claims is an AI claims agent that helps consumers get paid for

every corporate violation impacting them — data breaches, privacy

violations, antitrust, and more. We've processed 65,000+ claims, with

projected consumer recovery of $75M+.

Chariot builds technology to challenge the status quo. We take bold swings

at the system to ascertain truth from stories, even if that means drawing

legal/PR fire from established actors who are territorial and profit from

the status quo.

As operators, we pride ourselves on our ethics, resilience, and humanity.

With each turn, we emerge smarter, better prepared, and with more insiders

who share our mission to build a better system. We're already working with

20+ law firms, including several among the five most active complex

litigation firms in the country.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Technical Product Manager who can both shape what we

build and drive it through to launch. You'll own initiatives end-to-end

across a fast-moving, early-stage company. This role wears both hats:

hands-on product work (discovery, specs, prioritization, metrics) and the

delivery side (timelines, cross-functional coordination, launch readiness).

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

  • Own a product area end-to-end: defining the problem and opportunity, deciding what we build and when — including AI elements: prompt and eval design, quality thresholds, human-in-the-loop review

  • Write specs engineers can easily build from: data models, transitions, edge cases, UI/UX suggestions, high-level test cases

  • Own all success metrics post-launch (basic data analysis and SQL fluency ideal)

  • Run delivery across multiple workstreams: timelines, dependencies, and launch readiness, keeping things moving without heavy process

  • Manage and prioritize the backlog to keep Linear organized

  • Keep cross-functional teams aligned (Legal Strategy, Engineering, Design, Ops, Marketing) — be the person who knows the status of everything and communicates it

  • Ensure go-live readiness by creating and executing the launch plan so launches are clean and learnings fold back into the next iteration

WHO YOU ARE

  • 5+ years in product, including time owning a technical surface (platform, data, infra, or AI) with a track record of shipping software end-to-end

  • Highly organized with strong prioritization and stakeholder communication; nothing falls through the cracks

  • Detail-oriented with a strong operational and organizational mindset

  • Hands-on — able to define the plan and do the work to execute it

  • Comfortable with ambiguity and self-directed in a fast-moving startup; you don't wait to be told what to do

  • Familiar with agile ways of working (Scrum/Kanban) and PM tools (Linear, Airtable, Retool, Notion)

  • Can read an API spec, reason about data models and system boundaries, and hold your own in an architecture discussion with engineers

  • Experience with experimentation and product analytics — funnel analysis, A/B tests; PostHog, Amplitude, Mixpanel or similar

  • Bonus: experience in a regulated industry — legal, healthcare, or finance

WHY JOIN NOW

  • Massive greenfield to build meaningful products that hold corporations accountable, in an era of unchecked corporate greed and weakening regulatory oversight

  • Competitive salary, equity, and benefits in a fast-growing, high-impact startup

  • Great vibes, sharp teammates, mission-led culture

  • 2–4 offsites per year in beautiful, cultural destinations; expenses covered for you and a +1

jobs.title: [External] Associate Attorney (Consumer Protection / Complex Litigation)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We're looking for a CA-barred litigation associate to join a DC/AZ law firm that initiates lawsuits against defendant companies across consumer protection and complex litigation verticals.

About Chariot Claims

Chariot Claims is an AI claims agent that helps consumers get paid for every corporate violation impacting them — data breaches, privacy violations, antitrust, UDTP, and more. Chariot has processed 125,000+ claims and works with 20+ law firms, including several among the five most active complex litigation firms in the country.

Law firms rely on Chariot to find the right claimants and handle data/operational complexity, so they can focus on what they do best: litigating.

About the Opportunity

This opportunity is ideal for a mid-career plaintiff-side litigator who wants to bring justice at scale by leveraging technology partners, notably Chariot Claims.

Primary responsibility

  • Work closely with the Mensch team to fine-comb demand letters — carefully reviewing drafts for statutory accuracy, factual citations, theory alignment, ToS conformity, and state coverage before they go out at scale

  • QA notice batches and claimant communications pre-send

Additional responsibilities

  • Partner with co-counsel to run plaintiff-side mass arbitration campaigns end-to-end: pre-suit demands, notices of dispute, AAA/JAMS filings, IDRs, and settlement negotiations

  • Serve as a substantive authority on case strategy, redlines, and filings

  • Evaluate and validate new case theories across consumer protection, privacy, UDTP, data breach, false advertising, and complex litigation verticals

  • Help refine the case evaluation playbook — design the framework, run reviews, and codify it for scale and repeatability

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Chariot's Legal Ops, Data, and Engineering teams to sharpen case pipelines and demand letter quality

Ideal background

  • JD and active bar membership in at least one U.S. jurisdiction (preferably CA)

  • ~5 years of complex litigation experience at a reputable law firm — Big Law or a well-regarded complex lit / plaintiffs' boutique (mass arbitration experience not required)

  • Direct experience with one or more of: consumer protection, UDTP, privacy/wiretapping, data breach, or false advertising theories is a plus

  • Strong attention to detail and comfort doing deep, careful review of legal drafts

  • Tech-inclined; comfortable using AI tools, legal tooling, and automation to move faster

  • Deadline-driven, organized, and pragmatic; able to make calls quickly without losing rigor

  • Mission-oriented and wants to hold corporations accountable

jobs.title: Staff Engineer, Verticalized AI
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Location: Remote / Hybrid (NYC/SF)

Position Type: Full-time / Contract (Flexible)

 

About the Role

We're hiring a Staff Engineer to own Chariot's AI: the systems that originate cases and that find, for each person, the claims they're owed. This is the AI core of the product, and you'll build the team, fullstack and ML, around it.

We're building a verticalized factory for claims. AI is what lets it scale: it lets us originate cases and match people to them continuously, with humans reviewing where judgment matters, so everyday people recover what they're owed.

This role is perfect for someone who's analytical, creative, and execution-driven. You thrive in fast-paced environments, love rapid experimentation, and know how to take an idea from prototype to a production system the rest of the team can build on.

Bonus: if you've worked in a regulated industry such as legal, healthcare, or finance.

 

About Chariot Claims

Chariot Claims is an AI claims agent that helps consumers get paid for every corporate violation impacting them: data breaches, privacy violations, antitrust, and more. We've processed 65,000+ claims, with projected consumer recovery of $75M+.

Chariot builds technology to challenge the status quo. We take bold swings at the system to ascertain truth from stories, even if that means drawing legal/PR fire from established actors who are territorial and profit from the status quo.

As operators, we pride ourselves on our ethics, resilience, and humanity. With each turn, we emerge smarter, better prepared, and with more insiders who share our mission to build a better system. We're already working with 20+ law firms, including several among the five most active complex litigation firms in the country.

 

What You'll Own

  • Own the agent systems that source and assemble cases, with human-in-the-loop review that raises quality and throughput.

  • Own the systems that match people to the claims they're owed, from sources they've explicitly permissioned, with consent and privacy as first principles.

  • Build the evaluation and quality infrastructure that keeps agent behavior measurable and reliable in production.

  • Own the cost and performance of AI at scale as an engineering target.

  • Contribute to shared platform foundations that make the whole team faster, including internal tooling, MCPs, and agent harnesses.

  • Recruit, vet, and grow the engineers, fullstack and ML, on this team.

 

How You'll Work (AI-Native)

  • AI-native, not AI-assisted. You build with coding harnesses and agents in the loop every day, and you push the frontier of what they can do for the team.

  • You treat internal tooling as product. You build the MCPs, harnesses, evals, and human interfaces that make the whole team faster, for internal ops and external users alike.

  • You make product calls autonomously. You've shipped products end-to-end and can decide what to build and why without waiting to be told, then defend it with evidence.

  • Autonomous and collaborative. You run your vertical like an owner and still pull in the same direction as the rest of the company.

 

Who You Are

  • Experience building and shipping production software, at staff-level technical scope.

  • A track record of shipping products end-to-end: you've owned the outcome, not just the code.

  • Strong product instincts and a bias toward action; comfortable making informed product decisions on your own.

  • Early-stage experience (Series A or earlier).

  • You've built and grown a team, or are clearly ready to; you'll be hiring and leading from day one.

  • Bonus: experience taking LLM agent systems to production, including human-in-the-loop review and evaluation; comfort owning both the ML and the product surface around it.

  • Stack: Python and Go, modern LLM / agent tooling, AWS.

 

Why Join Now

  • Massive greenfield to own the AI core of the factory: the systems that originate cases and find people the claims they're owed. Help scale holding corporations accountable (in an era of unchecked corporate greed and weakening regulatory oversight).

  • Competitive salary, equity, and benefits package in a fast-growing, high-impact startup.

  • Collaborative, smart, humble, mission-driven, high-vibes team that loves music.

  • 2-4 off-sites per year in beautiful, cultural destinations; expenses covered for you and a +1.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Location: Remote / Hybrid (NYC/SF)

Position Type: Full-Time / Contract (Flexible)

 

About the Role

We're hiring a Staff Engineer to own Chariot's consumer platform: everything that turns a one-time claimant into an engaged member who keeps finding cases worth joining. You'll own the engagement, community, education, and referral surfaces, and help expand the range of cases people can join. This is greenfield community, content, and growth-loop product, and you'll build the team around it.

We're building a verticalized factory for claims: a system that turns corporate wrongdoing into recovery for everyday people. The consumer platform is how that factory compounds: engaged people surface new cases, refer others, and learn to tell a strong claim from a weak or fraudulent one.

This role is perfect for someone who's analytical, creative, and execution-driven. You thrive in fast-paced environments, love rapid experimentation, and know how to take an idea from prototype to a production system the rest of the team can build on.

Bonus: if you've worked in a regulated industry such as legal, healthcare, or finance.

  • Expand the range of case types people can discover and join.

  • Build the community surfaces where people surface, discuss, and rally around potential cases.

  • Build the education layer that helps people understand how claims work, what makes a strong case, and how to participate responsibly.

  • Build referral and growth loops that turn engaged members into a distribution channel.

  • Own trust and safety for community surfaces, including moderation and fraud deterrence.

  • Contribute to shared platform foundations that make the whole team faster, including internal tooling, MCPs, and agent harnesses.

  • Strong product instincts and a bias toward action; comfortable making informed product decisions on your own.

  • Early-stage experience (Series A or earlier).

  • You've built and grown a team, or are clearly ready to; you'll be hiring and leading from day one.

(TikTok / Reels / Shorts / LinkedIn)**

About Us

Chariot helps people claim money they’re owed when companies violate their rights. It’s serious work, but we keep it real and relatable. Now we want to reach millions more organically with smart, fun, and share-worthy content across every social channel.


The Role

We’re looking for a creative, trend-savvy Social Media Associate to own strategy, ideation, and execution for all of Chariot’s social platforms. You’ll manage our content calendar, brainstorm fun campaign ideas, and coordinate with influencers and creators to bring bigger content to life. You're just as comfortable in front of the camera as behind it; we want someone who can organize ideas and hop on camera for quick TikToks/Reels when needed.

You’ll thrive here if you…

  • Know what’s trending on TikTok, IG, and how to spin it for a brand.

  • Can wrangle a content calendar like a pro.

  • Love organizing and executing small ideas quickly.

  • Can track performance, test new formats, and adjust based on what’s working.

  • Are comfortable replying to DMs/comments in a voice that’s fun, smart, and true to us.

  • You’ve played around with AI content tools and can generate content quickly

  • Have experience/success with social media growth loops

  • Bonus: You’ve had content go viral before and think you can do the same with ours!


What you’ll do

📆 Run our weekly content calendar across TikTok, IG, FB, X, Threads, BlueSky, LinkedIn

💡 Plan fun, fresh ideas in-house and manage UGC/influencer content

🎥 Shoot and appear in quick-turn content yourself

📊 Track and report performance, test variations, and help iterate

💬 Reply to comments, DMs, and tags in our tone of voice

⚡️ Keep everything cohesive, on-brand, and aligned with broader campaigns

Why Join + Compensation

  • Hold corporations accountable (in an era of unchecked corporate greed and weakening regulatory oversight)

  • Great vibes, sharp teammates, mission-led culture

  • Paid hourly plus bonuses for high-performing content

  • Fully remote and async-friendly

  • Potential for full-time Social Media Marketing role

jobs.title: General Counsel
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Location: Remote (Hybrid - Brooklyn, NY)
Position Type: Full-Time / Part'Time / Contract (Flexible)

About the role

Chariot is an AI-native consumer protection platform that originates, underwrites, and resolves mass arbitration and class claims at scale. We operate at the intersection of consumer litigation, structured finance, and legal services regulation — which makes this a broader GC seat than the title usually implies.

This role reports to the CEO and owns the company's legal function end to end; you’ll be the business’s lawyer. This role is not running litigation strategy or the case/claimant docket, but does require familiarity with litigation.

What you'll own

  • Commercial contracting: vendor, data, partnership, and enterprise agreements

  • Corporate and financing work: equity financings, cap table hygiene, board materials, option grants, and cross-border employment questions

  • Litigation finance: negotiating and administering debt facilities

  • Regulatory / Ethics: legal-services regulatory regimes that govern alternative business structures

  • Privacy and data: policy drafting, CCPA/CPRA and state privacy compliance, vendor DPAs, and handling claimant data at volume

  • Outside counsel management across corporate, litigation, ethics, and regulatory specialties

  • Defense-side correspondence: triaging cease-and-desists and threatened litigation from large-firm counsel

  • Company-side risk: employment, IP, marketing review, and AI governance for our own products

What we're looking for

  • 7–15 years of experience, with a mix of top-tier firm and in-house time

  • Real transactional and corporate depth

  • Litigation experience or exposure sufficient to read a complaint, pressure-test a claim theory.

  • Comfort operating without precedent; in a business model that doesn't map cleanly onto existing categories. Highly curious and learning/growth-driven.

Bonus

  • Existing relationships with in-house legal leadership at Fortune 500 companies

  • Experience at a high-growth startup through a priced round

  • Prior work in debt financing

jobs.title: Senior Product, GTM, and Channel Partnerships - IC, Senior
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Chariot

Chariot is an AI-native consumer protection platform. We originate, underwrite, and resolve mass arbitration and class action claims at scale — turning “a company wronged you and you’ll never do anything about it” into real money back in people’s pockets. Our litigation engine (CaseGen) lets us run campaigns against household-name companies with a speed and unit economics the plaintiffs’ bar has never had.

Most consumers never learn they’re owed money, and the places where they’d most naturally find out — the fintech, credit, and personal-finance apps they already trust — aren’t surfacing it. The company that owns that embedded layer owns the category. That’s this role.

The role

You’ll build Chariot’s distribution flywheel: embedding claim eligibility and intake into the products where millions of eligible consumers already are — think a credit-monitoring app, a neobank, a cashback or tax product surfacing “You may be owed $X from [campaign] — start your claim” inline, the way Credit Karma surfaces financial products. You own this end to end across three hats:

  • Product partnerships — define the surface partners actually integrate: the eligibility API, the intake SDK/co-branded flows, identity/data matching, claim-status webhooks. You’re the voice of the partner in our roadmap, working hand in hand with engineering so what we ship is genuinely embeddable.

  • GTM — build the offer and the motion: the economic model (rev-share, referral, co-marketing), the partner value prop (a new revenue line, member value, retention), the pitch, and the playbook that makes the second and tenth partner faster than the first. You’ll run both a self-serve/PLG lane for smaller integrators and a high-touch enterprise lane for the Credit-Karma-scale partners.

  • Channel — source, structure, negotiate, and close the partners themselves, then drive them to activation and real claimant volume. This is a carry-the-number seat, not a strategy seat.

What you’ll do

  • Land the first wave of lighthouse embedded partners across fintech, credit/identity monitoring, neobanks, cashback/loyalty, tax and financial-wellness, benefits/HR, and affinity platforms.

  • Shape the partner-facing product — eligibility checks, intake SDK, co-branded web flows, data/identity matching — in tight partnership with engineering, and own its roadmap.

  • Design the deal architecture: economics, data-sharing and compliance terms, attribution, and SLAs that are genuinely win-win.

  • Build the repeatable integration + economic model so onboarding a new partner goes from a bespoke project to a known path.

  • Stand up both motions — a lighter self-serve integration path and an enterprise motion for the largest partners — and instrument the funnel from intro to live volume.

  • Partner internally with legal/QC, ops, and campaign leads so distribution respects the realities of how claims are run and resolved.

  • Be the market-facing owner of distribution in investor, partner, and ecosystem conversations.

Who you are

  • You’ve built an ecosystem from zero. You’ve personally stood up an app/API/integration partner program and scaled it — not inherited a mature one. (Someone who’s taken a partner ecosystem from a handful to hundreds, or built an API/distribution business from scratch, is exactly right.)

  • You’re fluent in embedded and API-led distribution — SDKs, integrations, co-branded flows, channel and GSI programs — and you understand the product mechanics, not just the deal.

  • You span product, GTM, and BD naturally. You can sit with engineering on an API contract in the morning and negotiate rev-share with a partner’s CRO in the afternoon, and you see the 360° business on both sides of the table.

  • You have founder/operator DNA. You’ve built something (ideally founded and/or sold a company), you’re comfortable in ambiguity, and you default to action over process.

  • You run both PLG and SLG motions and know when each applies.

  • You’re a deal-maker — you structure win-win economics and close partnerships others think are impossible, with the follow-through to take them from signed to live.

  • You’re relationship-first and creative — people trust you fast, and you find the non-obvious structure that unlocks a deal.

  • 10+ years in partnerships/GTM, several at the senior/leadership level, with real early-stage reps.

Bonus

  • Distribution experience in fintech or consumer finance (the Credit-Karma-adjacent surface) or another regulated, consumer-money-movement space.

  • Legaltech / regtech exposure, or comfort operating where compliance is a first-class constraint.

  • Data partnerships / identity matching experience, or two-sided marketplace / network-effects distribution.

Logistics

  • Location: Remote (US) / Hybrid (NYC, DC, SF, LA)

  • Comp: Competitive base + meaningful early equity + partnership-outcome-linked upside.

  • Reports to: CEO.

You’ll build Chariot’s distribution flywheel: embedding claim eligibility and intake into the products where millions of eligible consumers already are — think a credit-monitoring app, a neobank, a cashback or tax product surfacing “You may be owed $X from [campaign] — start your claim” inline, the way Credit Karma surfaces financial products. You own this end to end across three hats:

 - Product partnerships — define the surface partners actually integrate: the eligibility API, the intake SDK/co-branded flows, identity/data matching, claim-status webhooks. You’re the voice of the partner in our roadmap, working hand in hand with engineering so what we ship is genuinely embeddable.

 - GTM — build the offer and the motion: the economic model (rev-share, referral, co-marketing), the partner value prop (a new revenue line, member value, retention), the pitch, and the playbook that makes the second and tenth partner faster than the first. You’ll run both a self-serve/PLG lane for smaller integrators and a high-touch enterprise lane for the Credit-Karma-scale partners.

 - Channel — source, structure, negotiate, and close the partners themselves, then drive them to activation and real claimant volume. This is a carry-the-number seat, not a strategy seat.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Land the first wave of lighthouse embedded partners across fintech, credit/identity monitoring, neobanks, cashback/loyalty, tax and financial-wellness, benefits/HR, and affinity platforms.

 - Shape the partner-facing product — eligibility checks, intake SDK, co-branded web flows, data/identity matching — in tight partnership with engineering, and own its roadmap.

 - Design the deal architecture: economics, data-sharing and compliance terms, attribution, and SLAs that are genuinely win-win.

 - Build the repeatable integration + economic model so onboarding a new partner goes from a bespoke project to a known path.

 - Stand up both motions — a lighter self-serve integration path and an enterprise motion for the largest partners — and instrument the funnel from intro to live volume.

 - Partner internally with legal/QC, ops, and campaign leads so distribution respects the realities of how claims are run and resolved.

 - Be the market-facing owner of distribution in investor, partner, and ecosystem conversations.


WHO YOU ARE

 - You’ve built an ecosystem from zero. You’ve personally stood up an app/API/integration partner program and scaled it — not inherited a mature one. (Someone who’s taken a partner ecosystem from a handful to hundreds, or built an API/distribution business from scratch, is exactly right.)

 - You’re fluent in embedded and API-led distribution — SDKs, integrations, co-branded flows, channel and GSI programs — and you understand the product mechanics, not just the deal.

 - You span product, GTM, and BD naturally. You can sit with engineering on an API contract in the morning and negotiate rev-share with a partner’s CRO in the afternoon, and you see the 360° business on both sides of the table.

 - You have founder/operator DNA. You’ve built something (ideally founded and/or sold a company), you’re comfortable in ambiguity, and you default to action over process.

 - You run both PLG and SLG motions and know when each applies.

 - You’re a deal-maker — you structure win-win economics and close partnerships others think are impossible, with the follow-through to take them from signed to live.

 - You’re relationship-first and creative — people trust you fast, and you find the non-obvious structure that unlocks a deal.

 - 10+ years in partnerships/GTM, several at the senior/leadership level, with real early-stage reps.


BONUS

 - Distribution experience in fintech or consumer finance (the Credit-Karma-adjacent surface) or another regulated, consumer-money-movement space.
